source_text: Κἀγὼ ἐλθὼν πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί, ἦλθον οὐ καθ’ ὑπεροχὴν λόγου ἢ σοφίας καταγγέλλων ὑμῖν τὸ ⸀μαρτύριον τοῦ θεοῦ.
english_snapshot: And I[a], when I came to you, brothers, did not come with lofty speech or wisdom[b], proclaiming to you the testimony of God.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read mystery of God.

source_text: παραδοῦναι τὸν τοιοῦτον τῷ Σατανᾷ εἰς ὄλεθρον τῆς σαρκός, ἵνα τὸ πνεῦμα σωθῇ ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ ⸀κυρίου.
english_snapshot: to hand such a man over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh[b][a], so that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'of our Lord Jesus' or 'of the Lord Jesus' instead of simply 'of the Lord.'

source_text: εἰ δὲ ὁ ἄπιστος χωρίζεται, χωριζέσθω· οὐ δεδούλωται ὁ ἀδελφὸς ἢ ἡ ἀδελφὴ ἐν τοῖς τοιούτοις, ἐν δὲ εἰρήνῃ κέκληκεν ⸀ἡμᾶς ὁ θεός.
english_snapshot: But if the unbeliever separates[a], let him separate. The brother or the sister is not enslaved in such cases[c][b], but God has called us in peace.

source_text: Ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἐν πᾶσιν ἡ γνῶσις· τινὲς δὲ τῇ ⸀συνηθείᾳ ⸂ἕως ἄρτι τοῦ εἰδώλου⸃ ὡς εἰδωλόθυτον ἐσθίουσιν, καὶ ἡ συνείδησις αὐτῶν ἀσθενὴς οὖσα μολύνεται.
english_snapshot: But not everyone has this knowledge[a]. Some, through familiarity with the idol until now, eat it as food sacrificed to an idol, and their conscience, being weak[b], is defiled.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'conscience of the idol' or have related variation in this clause; the main text follows the SBLGNT reading.

source_text: μηδὲ ἐκπειράζωμεν τὸν ⸀Χριστόν, ⸀καθώς τινες αὐτῶν ἐπείρασαν, καὶ ὑπὸ τῶν ὄφεων ⸀ἀπώλλυντο.
english_snapshot: Nor should we put Messiah to the test[b][a], as some of them tested him and were being destroyed by the snakes.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'the Lord' instead of 'the Messiah' (or 'Christ').

source_text: καὶ εὐχαριστήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ ⸀εἶπεν· Τοῦτό μού ἐστιν τὸ σῶμα τὸ ὑπὲρ ⸀ὑμῶν· τοῦτο ποιεῖτε εἰς τὴν ἐμὴν ἀνάμνησιν.
english_snapshot: And after giving thanks[a], he broke it and said, “This is my body, which is for you[b]. Keep doing this in remembrance of me.”

signals.text: Some manuscripts add 'broken' after 'for you': 'This is my body, which is broken for you.'

source_text: ὁ γὰρ ἐσθίων καὶ ⸀πίνων κρίμα ἑαυτῷ ἐσθίει καὶ πίνει μὴ διακρίνων τὸ ⸀σῶμα.
english_snapshot: For the one who eats and drinks eats and drinks judgment on himself[b][a], not discerning the body.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'the Lord's body' instead of 'the body.'

source_text: ⸂καὶ ἐὰν⸃ ψωμίσω πάντα τὰ ὑπάρχοντά μου, ⸄καὶ ἐὰν⸃ παραδῶ τὸ σῶμά μου, ἵνα ⸀καυθήσομαι, ἀγάπην δὲ μὴ ἔχω, οὐδὲν ὠφελοῦμαι.
english_snapshot: And if I give away all my possessions[a], and if I hand over my body so that I may be burned, but do not have love, I gain nothing.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'so that I may boast' instead of 'so that I may be burned.'

english_snapshot: But if anyone does not recognize this[b][a], he is not recognized.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read, 'if anyone is ignorant, let him be ignorant.' The adopted text reads, 'if anyone ignores this, he is ignored.'

source_text: καὶ καθὼς ἐφορέσαμεν τὴν εἰκόνα τοῦ χοϊκοῦ, ⸀φορέσομεν καὶ τὴν εἰκόνα τοῦ ἐπουρανίου.
english_snapshot: And just as we have borne the image of the man of dust[a], we will also bear the image of the heavenly man.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'let us also bear the image of the heavenly man.'

source_text: ἰδοὺ μυστήριον ὑμῖν λέγω· ⸀πάντες οὐ κοιμηθησόμεθα πάντες δὲ ἀλλαγησόμεθα,
english_snapshot: Behold[a], I tell you a mystery: we will not all sleep, but we will all be changed[b],

signals.text: A notable textual variant reads, in effect, 'we will all sleep, but we will not all be changed.' The main text follows the SBLGNT reading.

source_text: ποῦ σου, θάνατε, τὸ ⸂νῖκος; ποῦ σου, θάνατε, τὸ κέντρον⸃;
english_snapshot: Where[a], O death, is your victory? Where, O death, is your sting?

signals.text: Some manuscripts read, 'Where, O death, is your sting?' in the first clause, a reading reflected in the KJV and other traditional translations.
